To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Chemokines and chemokine receptors are expressed in CNS inflammatory processes, (b) the expression pattern of chemokine and chemokine receptor mRNA and protein is different in CNS demyelination in animal models and in humans, (c) chemokines and their cognate chemokine receptors regulate cellular infiltration in CNS demyelinatng disease in animal models and humans.
the chemokine receptor CCR2 mediates leukocyte recruitment to the CNS in the EAE model of multiple sclerosis and that this chemokine receptor plays an important role in human multiple sclerosis.

chemokines and their respective receptors are expressed and function in the CNS during inflammation, that chemokines are involved in the pathogenesis of CNS inflammation, and that chemokines may be useful targets in therapeutic intervention of inflammatory CNS disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemokine receptors and their ligands in CNS diseases.
the role of the chemokines and their cognate receptors in the regulation of leukocyte trafficking to the central nervous system in inflammatory disease.

the chemokine receptor CXCR2, which mediates the recruitment of neutrophils and lymphocytes into the CNS in the course of experimental allergic encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model for multiple sclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemokine and chemokine receptor system is involved in the pathogenesis of neuroinflammatory disorders.
the role of the chemokines and their respective receptors in CNS inflammation is not yet fully understood.
chemokines are involved in all stages of CNS inflammation, and that their role is not only to attract leukocytes into the CNS but to modulate their function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemokines and their corresponding receptors are expressed in a complex and overlapping pattern in the normal and pathologic CNS, and that the expression of these molecules is tightly regulated.
the chemokine receptor CXCR3 and the chemokines CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11, which are ligands for this receptor, are of particular importance for leukocyte infiltration of inflammatory CNS lesions.
chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) is involved in the development of experimental autoimmune encephalitis (EAE) and multiple sclerosis (MS) in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokines play a critical role in the pathogenesis and progression of MS and other neuroinflammatory disorders.
the chemokine systems is a major player in neuroinflammations and that it is involved at all levels of the disease.
chemokines are important in CNS inflammation and that they may represent novel targets for therapy.
